items.title: Document current ownership and non-duplication boundaries
items.context: Map milestone ledger, acceptanceBindings, verificationIntent, verificationEvidence, REVIEW completeness, and lifecycle gate ownership so the proposal cannot create a parallel truth source.
items.userSees: The current-state table shows milestone ledger, acceptanceBindings, verificationIntent, evidence, and REVIEW completeness as distinct existing owners, and explicitly says no standalone acceptance-matrix truth source will be created.

happy.desc: Inspect the plan current-state ownership table -> milestone ledger, proofstory acceptanceBindings, checklist verificationIntent, verificationEvidence, REVIEW completeness, and lifecycle gates each have a distinct existing owner and responsibility; WHY: proves the proposal starts from canonical facts instead of an invented model.

Trace the proposed acceptance matrix/view back to existing artifacts -> it is explicitly derived from the confirmed milestone ledger plus proofstory acceptanceBindings and cannot be independently authored; WHY: preserves one source of truth.

edge.desc: Audit ordinary single-outcome, milestone-triggered, and legacy stories in the boundary section -> the plan distinguishes optional milestone data, candidate versus confirmed ledgers, and observe/warn/enforce behavior without retroactively inventing obligations; WHY: prevents boundary claims from over-applying the strict path.

Audit the documentation-only scope and future-runtime boundary -> current implemented behavior, proposed future commands/artifacts, and explicit non-goals are labeled separately; WHY: prevents a plan from being misread as shipped gate capability.

adversarial.desc: Search for any standalone writable acceptance matrix, duplicated criterion store, or second completion ledger -> none is proposed, and any matrix is declared a read-only derived rendering with canonical source references; WHY: detects parallel truth-source drift.

Challenge conflicting ownership or completion language -> milestone progress cannot satisfy verification evidence, REVIEW, lifecycle DONE, Authority DONE, or production readiness, and local artifacts cannot overclaim those states; WHY: blocks false equivalence between planning facts and completion proof.

items.title: Specify acceptance topology and both lifecycle checks
items.context: Define auditable schema fields, authority/freshness semantics, totality rules, PLAN-to-DEV structural checking, DEV-to-REVIEW executable checking, failure codes, and derived rendering.
items.userSees: The document contains a field-level acceptance topology schema and deterministic PLAN-to-DEV acceptance_topology_check plus DEV-to-REVIEW pre_review_check algorithms, including authority, freshness, mutation polarity, transcript, and failure-code rules.

happy.desc: Audit the field-level acceptance topology schema -> each acceptance claim identifies canonical source/claim, producer, consumer, positive proof, mutation proof, transcript or receipt reference, authority boundary, temporal role, and freshness bindings; WHY: makes every proof edge explicit and auditable.

Walk the specified PLAN-to-DEV acceptance_topology_check and DEV-to-REVIEW pre_review_check algorithms on a complete example -> the structural check validates graph totality before implementation while the executable check requires current admissible proof before REVIEW, with deterministic pass/warn/block outputs and named failure codes; WHY: proves the two gates own different lifecycle questions.

edge.desc: Evaluate topology totality for optional claims, one-to-many producers or consumers, not-applicable edges, and documentation-only stories -> the plan defines explicit justified handling without silently dropping required nodes or forcing executable evidence during PLAN; WHY: covers legitimate non-uniform graphs.

Evaluate freshness cases where materialHash matches, materialHash drifts while signed storyFilesHash matches, storyFilesHash changes, or legacy records lack storyFilesHash -> the plan preserves strict fallback, mandatory re-attestation advisory, and stale rejection semantics without silent rebinding; WHY: aligns proposed checks with existing freshness truth.

adversarial.desc: Substitute positive-only evidence, inverted mutation polarity, a transcript unrelated to the asserted claim, or caller-writable authority metadata -> pre_review_check rejects the edge with specific reason codes and cannot promote local or diagnostic output to Authority proof; WHY: prevents proof-shaped but semantically invalid evidence from passing.

Remove a required producer-consumer edge or describe a gate fact only in prose -> acceptance_topology_check fails closed and the plan requires CLI/handler enforcement plus process-fact registry and contract-verifier updates for every gate-consumed fact; WHY: prevents prompt-only or partial-graph bypass.

items.title: Specify implementation waves, negative controls, rollout, and audit rubric
items.context: Produce bounded implementation stories, exact likely code touchpoints, observe-warn-enforce compatibility, migration behavior, mutation tests, success metrics, risks, open decisions, and a reviewer audit checklist.
items.userSees: The document ends with bounded implementation waves, an observe-warn-enforce migration, positive and negative test matrices, process-fact obligations, success metrics, risks, open decisions, and an audit checklist the user can mark pass or request changes against.
